title: Federal Register: Commercial Driver's License Drug and Alcohol Clearinghouse, final rule (81 FR 87686)

history.reason: Source read directly on the access date; findings transcribed from the document.

publisher: U.S. Department of Transportation, FMCSA (via GovInfo / Federal Register)
source_type: Government final rule with regulatory impact and regulatory flexibility analysis
reliability: Government document; the issuing agency (FMCSA) is also the party imposing and administering the requirement. Figures are ex ante estimates made in 2016, not measured burden.
findings: FMCSA's final regulatory flexibility analysis treats motor carriers of property with 146 or fewer power units as small; it estimates over 99 percent of interstate property carriers with recent activity are small, about 515,000 of 520,000 active motor carriers.

FMCSA states ninety-nine percent of motor carriers, MROs, C/TPAs and SAPs are most likely small entities, and that it identified no significant alternatives that could lessen small-entity burden without compromising the statutory mandate.

The information collection burden is estimated at about 1.86 million hours annually (table total 1,864,000 hours over 11,039,655 instances). Examples: annual queries 5,200,000 instances at 10 minutes (867,000 hours); pre-employment queries 1,996,328 at 10 minutes (333,000 hours); register/familiarize/verify 793,000 instances at 20 or 10 minutes (155,000 hours); driver consents and verifications 2,357,328 at 10 minutes (393,000 hours). Tasks are assumed to be done by bookkeeping clerks (employers) or drivers.

FMCSA's RIA estimates about $154 million annual cost against $196 million annual crash-reduction benefit, including $29 million of employee time for annual queries, $11 million for pre-employment queries, and $24 million of Clearinghouse access fees (fee levels were not set in this rule).

The rule requires an owner-operator who employs himself or herself as a driver to designate a C/TPA to handle employer reporting; FMCSA states this should not create new burdens because such owner-operators already must join a C/TPA-managed testing pool under 382.103(b).

In response to a commenter who said first-time registration alone would take more than 10 minutes, FMCSA disagreed that its 20-minute registration and familiarization estimate was too low, saying much registration would be automated.
limitations: Row labels of the burden table were matched to numbers from a layout-preserving PDF extraction; a reviewer should re-check the table.
The power-unit-to-revenue conversion for the small-carrier threshold uses a 2014-dollar proxy and the then-current SBA size standard; neither was re-checked.
Fee levels, current Clearinghouse functionality and later amendments (for example 2021 State licensing agency rule) were not read here.
Does not measure actual time spent, errors, or costs borne by owner-operators or very small carriers.
